label: Top Collar
description: A contrast top collar replaces the standard matching collar cloth with a different material — most commonly a velvet, a contrasting colour, or a contrasting texture — creating a clearly visible band of alternative fabric at the back of the neck and along the undercollar seam where it frames the face. The velvet collar in particular has a long history in formal English dress, seen on chesterfield overcoats and Edwardian dress coats, and its addition to a suit jacket elevates the garment from purely functional tailoring to a statement of aesthetic refinement. Even a tonal contrast — for example, a dark grey velvet on a charcoal wool suit — adds depth and dimensionality at the jacket's highest and most visible point.
